_comment: Hardware specifications. Every field carries a source and a confidence tag. Filter for confidence != 'published' to generate the limitations section.

_confidence_levels.published: Stated directly by SpaceX or in a peer-reviewed paper. Trust it.
_confidence_levels.derived: Computed from a published relative claim. Defensible, but must be labelled as derived wherever it appears.
_confidence_levels.estimated: Reasonable inference from geometry or standard convention. Sweep as uncertain.
_confidence_levels.disputed: Sources conflict materially. MUST be swept as a parameter, never assumed.

mass_kg.source: Baruah et al. 2024 gives 227 kg; secondary sources give 260-303 kg
mass_kg.action: Use 227 kg for validation to match the paper. Sweep the full range for project runs.

ram_area_knife_edge_m2.source: Baruah et al. 2024 uses 1.00 m2 as lower bound; secondary sources suggest 0.3-0.7 m2
ram_area_knife_edge_m2.action: Use 1.00 m2 for validation. Note that independent sources agree on this value far better than on the nominal-attitude area.

ram_area_nominal_m2.source: Source A gives 0.5-1.5 m2; Source B gives 5-6 m2. A 4-10x disagreement.
ram_area_nominal_m2.action: DO NOT pick a value. This parameter must be swept. Note in the writeup that the Feb 2022 validation does not depend on it, since the satellites were in knife-edge attitude.
ram_area_nominal_m2._note: Source B's own description contradicts its number: it says the array is 'feathered parallel to the velocity vector to minimize drag', which implies a small area.

ram_area_max_m2.action: Upper bound for the validation sweep.

thrust_n.source: Computed as 0.170 N / 2.4, from SpaceX's claim that the v2 mini thruster produces 2.4x the thrust of the v1.5 unit
thrust_n.action: Label as DERIVED wherever it appears. Do not claim SpaceX published this number.

isp_s.source: Computed as 2500 s / 1.5, from SpaceX's claim of 1.5x specific impulse improvement

bus_dimensions_m.source: Secondary reporting; sources give 2.8x1.3 m and 3.0x1.5 m

geometry._comment: Parametric geometry for the Phase 8 projected-area solver. Dimensions only -- the ram AREAS elsewhere in this file stay as they are, and are what the solver is checked against rather than derived from.

bus_length_m.source: Secondary reporting gives 2.8x1.3 m and 3.0x1.5 m for the chassis.
bus_length_m.action: Sweep both. The choice moves broadside chassis area from 3.64 to 4.50 m2, which straddles Baruah's published 4.48 m2 maximum -- see the _finding note below.

bus_width_m.source: Paired with bus_length_m; same two sources.
bus_width_m.action: Sweep with bus_length_m as a pair, not independently.

bus_thickness_m.source: Not published. Inferred from the flat-pack stacking density: ~60 v1.5 satellites fit a Falcon 9 fairing stack.
bus_thickness_m.action: Sweep. Sets the knife-edge area almost single-handedly.

solar_array_span_m.source: Derived: Spaceflight Now (2023-02-26) gives ~11 m end-to-end with the single panel extended; subtracting the 2.8-3.0 m chassis leaves ~8 m of array.
solar_array_span_m.action: Label as DERIVED from a span figure, not a published array dimension.

solar_array_chord_m.source: Assumed equal to the chassis width; not independently sourced.
solar_array_chord_m.action: Weakest number in this block. Sweep it.

solar_array_thickness_m.source: Standard thin-film/rigid array panel thickness. Non-zero on purpose: a zero-thickness plate presents exactly zero area edge-on and would flatter the knife-edge result.

geometry._cross_check_power: Array area 8.0 x 1.4 = 11.2 m2. At ~200 W/m2 for space-grade cells this gives ~2.2 kW, consistent with reported v1.5 power. The estimate is not free-floating.
geometry._finding: The solver reproduces Baruah et al.'s published 4.48 m2 maximum ram area as a FACE-ON chassis area, not as a true broadside. Chassis face-on is 2.8x1.3 = 3.64 m2 or 3.0x1.5 = 4.50 m2; the latter agrees with 4.48 m2 to 0.45%. Two things follow. (1) The published 'maximum' appears to be the chassis face with the solar array feathered -- a genuine broadside including the array is ~15 m2, more than 3x larger. (2) It is not even the chassis's own geometric maximum: a box presents most area corner-on, giving 4.65 m2 for the same chassis, 3.3% above face-on. So 4.48 m2 is best read as 'chassis face-on, array feathered', which is consistent with the knife-edge attitude the February 2022 fleet was actually commanded into. See tests/test_geometry.py.

mass_kg.source: Secondary reporting. 800 kg initial, ~525 kg optimized.
mass_kg.action: Sweep the range. Mass strongly affects ballistic coefficient.

ram_area_knife_edge_m2.source: Two independent sources agree: 1.0-1.8 m2 and 1.2-1.5 m2
ram_area_knife_edge_m2.action: Reasonable agreement between sources. Use midpoint, sweep the range.

ram_area_nominal_m2.source: Source A gives 2.5-4.0 m2; Source B gives 11-12 m2
ram_area_nominal_m2.action: Sweep. Note that Source B's 11-12 m2 is simply the chassis face area (4.1 x 2.7 = 11.07 m2), which is a broadside orientation unlikely to be flown deliberately at low altitude.

thruster_type.source: SpaceX; first operational use of argon for electric propulsion in space

solar_array_area_m2.source: Two 52.5 m2 arrays. Both sources agree on 105 m2 total.
solar_array_area_m2._note: A figure of 116 m2 appeared in one source without explanation and is not used.

drag_coefficient_baseline.source: Standard convention for satellites in free-molecular flow. Used in NASA DAS, STK, and orbit determination work.
drag_coefficient_baseline.action: Use 2.2 for project runs, sweep 2.0-2.4 in Monte Carlo.

drag_coefficient_validation.source: Baruah et al. 2024, stated as a simplification for comparative analysis
drag_coefficient_validation.action: MUST be used for the validation case. See PHYSICS.md section 8, Test 4.

_cd_at_higher_altitude.note: One source quotes Cd = 2.4-2.45 at ~550 km. That figure is for a different altitude regime with different atmospheric composition and does not apply at 210 km. Not used.

reference_satellite._comment: Swarm C, used by Baruah et al. as a comparison case. Useful for a secondary validation.
reference_satellite.name: Swarm C
reference_satellite.action: Optional second validation target. The paper's synthetic ephemeris gave 25.02 m against 23.08 m observed. If time allows, reproducing this is a cheap extra credibility win at a different altitude.
